design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 0 (Ferreira household), difficulty meal_account_and_benefits, env_0078 (Calloway Creek ISD). Revision 3.

1. DRAW (draw_counts.py --task 0): {"task": 0, "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [5, 5, 5, 5]}. Placement: prepayment 5, cover 5, netting 5, inactive repayment 5.

2. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST
Marisol Ferreira asks how much to put on Lucia's meal account (grade 6, Ridgecrest Middle School, -47.00) so she is caught up and covered for a while, and she will pay it herself online. The quote may only be made after (a) the departed-balance cover from Tomas's inactive account (withdrew to a private school 2026-10-09, +88.55), which itself waits on (b) netting the idle part of Mateo's active account (Pecan Grove Elementary, a CEP campus, +56.90), and (c) the repayment payment due today on Rafael's inactive account (moved to another Texas district, -29.80). Every figure is computed on the world the earlier writes leave, from the district's published prices, its 2026-27 calendar and the account records.

3. SCOPE
Task 0 claims meals_ext_sibling_idle_netting, meals_ext_departed_charge_cover, meals_ext_inactive_repayment, meals_ext_prepayment_quote and their tools. Task 1 claims the CEP refund, the active-account repayment plan, the graduate rollover and the departure rollover. Scope tails keep each task's rules out of the other's world: the cover covers only a sibling withdrawn for a leaver reason other than moved_out_of_state / returned_to_home_country (graduates and out-of-state leavers follow the rollovers); the departure rollover only those two reasons; the graduate rollover only leaver reason graduated; the netting is made only as part of a departed-balance cover; the inactive plan only for inactive accounts; the active plan only for active accounts on a repayment request or a quote of the payment due today, and a one-deposit catch-up-and-fund-ahead request follows the prepayment (P-07 tails, both sides name each other).

4. PROBLEM-TREE CARD
root meals_ext_prepayment_quote (USER deposit on Lucia)
 <- meals_ext_departed_charge_cover: value_input, gate q_balance, action form. "The prepayment quote is fixed only after every cover owed to this student's account from the inactive account of a departed sibling in the household has been made." Opening: Tomas inactive +88.55, no transfer out. Skipping it: quote 174.25 instead of 88.80.
    <- meals_ext_sibling_idle_netting: value_input, gate c_balance, action form. "The cover amount is fixed only after the idle balance of each other active account of the household has been netted to the receiving account." Opening: Mateo +56.90, no transfer out. Skipping it: cover 91.60, above Tomas's 88.55, so none owed.
 <- meals_ext_inactive_repayment (USER deposit on Rafael): state_gate, state form. "A prepayment is not quoted until each inactive account of the household whose unpaid meal charges are at least the online deposit minimum carries a repayment payment posted on the day of the quote." Opening: Rafael -29.80, no deposit dated 2026-10-21.
VI edges 2 of 3. Order: netting, cover, (Rafael's payment commutes), prepayment. Owner=user: both deposits are the parent's own portal payments (owner_ruling (b)/(c)); stated in each rule. Tools validate format and existence only.

5. FACTOR CARDS (tier taken -> figure with that factor at baseline) and REALISM TAGS (realism_bar.md; coordinator ruling O-12: calendar x published prices is the plain amount basis of the quote, and of the cover and the netting keep because the parent states that purpose in the persona)
netting on Mateo, expected 6.15, all-baseline 0.00 (keep the parent asks for: Mateo's meals, milk and extra helpings through the end of next month):
 netting_card_hold (P, R2, multi-source): no returned deposit, card 2026-10-05 25.00 in the month -> held -> 31.15
 netting_keep_days (P, R3, one count): 7 left in October + November's 16 -> 23 -> 8.40 (standard 20)
 netting_keep_lunch (P, R1, enroll): enrolled campus Pecan Grove (CEP) -> 0.00 -> 0.00 (keep above the balance)
 netting_keep_milk (M, R1): milk rung up four times -> milk price every counted day -> 23.40
 netting_keep_second_meal (M, R1): second meals rung up twice -> 8.50 once -> 14.65
cover on Lucia, expected 85.45, all-baseline 56.35 (the parent asks: clear what Lucia owes and pay for her meals and extras for the rest of this month):
 cover_serving_days (P, R3): 7 -> 74.35 (standard five)
 cover_lunch (P, R1, enroll): Ridgecrest -> 3.45 -> 83.00
 cover_breakfast (P, R1): breakfasts in the month at Ridgecrest -> 2.10 -> 70.75
 cover_milk (M, R1): milk rung up twice -> 1.50 once -> 83.95
 cover_second_meal (M, R1): one second meal -> 4.25 once -> 81.20
inactive repayment on Rafael, expected 22.45, all-baseline 29.80:
 plan_size_installments (P, R5) -> 24.90; plan_up_front (M, R5) -> 10.00; plan_household_students (P, R6, enroll) -> 23.27; plan_school_calendar (P, R6) -> 23.27; plan_last_payment (P, R6) -> 21.96
prepayment on Lucia, expected 88.80, all-baseline 17.40:
 quote_serving_days (P, R3, one count): 23 -> 72.15; quote_lunch_charge (P, R1, enroll) -> 80.75; quote_breakfast (P, R1) -> 40.50; quote_milk (M, R1) -> 87.30; quote_second_meal (M, R1) -> 84.55
R6 tags (AMENDMENT 1, graded R6-WAIVED in revision 3): plan_household_students (key: household enrollment records in status enrolled), plan_school_calendar (key: the quote month), plan_last_payment (key: days from the latest online card deposit to the quote date, the end date counted). Minimal count 5 - 2 honest = 3.

6. BASE-INVARIANT CARD
Transfers: transfer_within_household (Lucia active, same household); amounts within the giving balances (6.15 <= 56.90; 85.45 <= 88.55). Deposits: deposit_to_open_account (Lucia active; Rafael inactive with unpaid charges); no_checks_after_return (Rafael's check returned 2026-09-09; no household check deposit afterwards; both payments online). No fee, interest or penalty anywhere (SP 46-2016).

7. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD: netting gives from Mateo (the only other active account) to Lucia; the cover gives from Tomas (the only departed sibling with a positive balance) to Lucia; Rafael's payment on Rafael only; the prepayment on Lucia only.

8. SEED: household profile 2026-07-14; four 2026-27 enrollment records (Lucia, Mateo enrolled; Tomas withdrawn 2026-10-09 private_school; Rafael withdrawn 2026-09-11 moved_to_other_texas_district); four Paid accounts opened 2026-08-03; transactions simulated school day by school day under base pricing (Pecan Grove CEP: lunches 0.00); deposits: Lucia online 08-10, 09-08; Mateo online 08-10, 10-05; Tomas online 08-10, 09-14; Rafael online 08-21 and a check 09-02 returned 09-09 (after which no household check deposit exists); notices generated by the base notice rules.

9. PERSONA: tired night-shift nurse; asks only for Lucia's amount and pays herself online; identity on request; other children only when asked; agrees to moving Tomas's and Mateo's money; pays Rafael's amount when told; ends after Lucia's payment.

10. XF TABLES
A1 factor reads: every factor owns its bindings (balance-basis and size factors recompute their balance with their own SUMs); no factor reads another factor's binding; assembly in plain bindings only. A2: one generic order sentence per policy. A3: the standard sentence and the balance sentence are the baseline; every schedule sentence belongs to one factor. A5: order sentences fix per-day sum, multiply by days, then the balance part / holds. A6 method pairs: milk and second meal (price on every counted day / last month's spending once / nothing: different inputs); up-front (all unpaid / returned amount / nothing). Breakfast is a parameter (secondary / elementary / nothing). The receiving balance is plain baseline arithmetic. One serving-day count per computation (F-06). A7: every rate x count pair has nonzero standards (day charge 3.10; days 20 or 5); T1 holds for all 20 factors (section 5); T2 holds (each factor moves the result with the others at baseline). A8: no factor reprices a posted line; no two factors cancel. A9: ladder text equals compute. A10: each factor document names the result it modifies only.
B1 edges: absent enrolled record -> elementary lunch; no breakfast/milk -> nothing; no card deposit -> plan "no online card deposit" tier; netting free amount below zero -> 0; quote <= 0 -> none; unpaid below the online minimum -> no portal payment; dates before 2026-08-12, in July 2026 or after 2027-05-27 handled by the days-left ladder. B2 decoys: Lucia/Mateo enrolled records vs Tomas's/Rafael's withdrawn records (status filter); XCOUNT counts only status enrolled (withdrawn records excluded); LATEST card deposit ignores the returned check and its source check (method filter), same-date ties return the same date. B3 whole-month windows match MONTHS; serving days from the stated 2026-27 calendar (weekdays less listed closures). B4 RND(x+1e-9) once at the end; all figures away from a half cent. B5 sweep 0 misses. B6 tool bodies enforce format and existence and write in their own bodies. C: no overwrite in task 0's policies. D1/D2: resolvers settle every engaged world; the inactive-repayment wait carries the online-minimum carve-out in the sentence. D4: transfers write both legs (same category).

11. STANDARD SOLUTION AND VERIFICATION
Writes: netting Mateo->Lucia 6.15; cover Tomas->Lucia 85.45; USER payment Rafael 22.45; USER prepayment Lucia 88.80. Run (/tmp/meal_account_and_benefits_0078/build/run_t0.py) reproduces every expected, baseline and sensitivity figure. Skips: no cover -> quote 174.25; no netting -> cover 91.60, above Tomas's 88.55 (not owed).

12. REVISION LOG
r1, r2: see earlier revisions (superseded). r3: tree kept; every computation rebuilt on published prices, the district calendar, record holds and plan terms; the named X1 mechanisms (milk two-fifths, buffers, notice-keyed restore/keep days, keep extras, charges-taken carve-outs, installment tapers by leaver reason/history/recency, letter up-front tier) removed; T0 world: Rafael's returned check replaces Lucia's, Mateo's check replaced by a card deposit, Tomas's second deposit.
r4: one serving-day count per computation; balance treatment moved into the standard; breakfast a parameter with distinct values; milk and second meals as methods (daily for regular buyers, last month's spending for occasional ones); persona states the cover's and the netting keep's purpose (coordinator ruling O-12); world: Lucia and Mateo buy second meals, Lucia an extra card deposit, Tomas's second deposit raised.
r5: wording only for task 0 - item schedules count purchases rung up (P-08); the cover's days ladder falls through to its standard five outside the 2026-27 year (F-07 class); figures unchanged.
r6: netting opening sentence made generic (renderer F2 class); netting tool docstring condition removed (F4); figures unchanged.
user_scenario: You are Marisol Ferreira, a hospital night-shift nurse in Calloway Creek, calling School Nutrition on your way home. Your daughter Lucia, who is in sixth grade at Ridgecrest Middle School, keeps getting negative-balance emails about her cafeteria account, and you want to fix it properly this time: you want to know how much you should put on Lucia's lunch account so she is caught up and covered for a while, and you will pay that yourself online through the district payment portal today, while you are on the phone. You say this plainly at the start, a little tired and apologetic. You do not know how the district handles money between your children's accounts, and you do not bring up your other children unless the agent asks about them. When the agent asks you to confirm who you are, you give your full name, Marisol Ferreira, your phone number 5125550121 and your date of birth, November 2, 1983 (1983-11-02); only if they ask for something more you give the last four digits of your ID, 2214. If the agent asks about your other children, you explain that you have four: Tomas, who was a tenth grader at Calloway Creek High School and switched to a private school after his last day on October 9; Rafael, who was in eighth grade at Ridgecrest Middle School and went to live with his father in Laredo in September; and Mateo, who is in second grade at Pecan Grove Elementary. If the agent explains that money sitting on Tomas's or Mateo's meal account should be moved over to Lucia's account first, you agree to it, saying it all ends up with your kids anyway: you want Tomas's leftover money to clear what Lucia owes and pay for her meals and anything else she buys for the rest of this month, and since Mateo eats free at Pecan Grove, you only want enough left on his account for his meals, milk and extra helpings through the end of next month, with the rest going to Lucia. If the agent tells you that something is still owed on Rafael's old account and has to be paid before Lucia's payment can be worked out, you sigh, say you did not realize, and say you will pay that online right now too; when the agent hands you that payment, you make it yourself through the portal for exactly the amount the agent tells you, and you read the confirmation number back if they ask. When the agent tells you the amount to put on Lucia's account and hands you that payment, you make it yourself through the portal for exactly that amount. If a figure the agent gives you sounds strange, you only say you trust them to check it against the account. Once Lucia's payment has gone through, you thank the agent, say you finally feel caught up, and end the call.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The netting must precede the cover: the cover's own rule says its amount is fixed only after the idle balances of the other active accounts have been netted to the receiving account (run: cover after netting 85.45; cover before netting 91.60, more than Tomas's 88.55, so none would be owed). The repayment payment touches only Rafael's account and neither the netting, the cover nor the prepayment reads Rafael's records, so it commutes with them; run: placing it first or third gives the same terminal state and the same 6.15 / 85.45 / 22.45 / 88.80. The prepayment comes last because both of its prerequisite sentences make it wait.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the cover, Lucia's balance at the quote is -40.85 and the prepayment computes 174.25 instead of 88.80; Tomas's account keeps 88.55.

Without the repayment payment, Rafael's inactive account keeps no 2026-10-21 deposit and stays at -29.80 (terminal state differs); the prepayment's own figure is unchanged, the edge is a state gate.
